question: Which three XML files are required for importing an EP1001 application package?
reference_answer: The required XML files are package-data.xml, application-body.xml, and ep-request.xml.

question: What fixed values must be used for the dtd-version and produced-by attributes in the <package-data> root element?
reference_answer: The dtd-version must be "1.0" and produced-by must be "applicant".

question: Which top-level elements inside <package-data> are always mandatory for an EP1001 submission?
reference_answer: The mandatory elements are <transmittal-info>, <signatories>, <application-request>, and <other-documents>.

question: Can the <signatories> section be omitted for an unsigned or draft EP1001 submission?
reference_answer: No, the <signatories> section must always be present, even if it contains a blank entry.

question: Which XML file is responsible for referencing all attached documents either directly or indirectly?
reference_answer: package-data.xml is responsible for referencing all attached documents, either directly or via referenced XML files.

question: Which elements must be present in application-body.xml for a successful EP1001 import even if they are empty?
reference_answer: The <description> and <claims> elements must be present even if they are empty.

question: Which section of application-body.xml is allowed to reference more than one technical document?
reference_answer: Only the drawings section may reference more than one document.

question: How is the id attribute of a <doc-page> element constructed?
reference_answer: It is constructed from a section code such as DESC, CLMS, ABST, or DRAW followed by a numeric counter.

question: Does the numeric suffix in filenames like SPECEPO-1.pdf correspond to a document section such as description or claims?
reference_answer: No, the numeric suffix only reflects the attachment order in OLF2.0 and does not correspond to a document section.

question: Which document code must be used for the EP1001 request XML file referenced in package-data.xml?
reference_answer: The document code is REQXML.

question: What information is stored inside an <ep-electronic-files> element in ep-request.xml?
reference_answer: It stores the document type code along with the applicant file name and the EPO file name.

question: If Italian is used as the filing language, which specification documents must be supplied?
reference_answer: Both the original Italian specification (SPECNONEPO) and its English translation (SPECTRANEPO) must be supplied.

question: Which attribute in the <ep-request> root element specifies the procedural language?
reference_answer: The procedural language is specified by the lang attribute.

question: How many <invention-title> elements are required in an EP1001 request and why?
reference_answer: Three are required, one each for English, French, and German.

question: Under what condition must the <priority-claims> element appear in ep-request.xml?
reference_answer: It must appear only when one or more priority claims are declared.

question: Should the <priority-claims> element appear if no priority is claimed?
reference_answer: No, it must not appear if no priority claims exist.

question: What is the minimum requirement if a <check-list> element is present in ep-request.xml?
reference_answer: It must contain at least a single empty <cl-request/> element.

question: Which document code is used for a single-file specification in an official EPO language?
reference_answer: The document code is SPECEPO.

question: What document code is used for a translated specification originating from a non-EPO language?
reference_answer: The document code is SPECTRANEPO.

question: What happens if an incorrect document code is used for an attachment?
reference_answer: The EPO receiving server will reject the files and not accept the submission.

question: Can the <application-body> element be omitted from package-data.xml for EP1001 submissions?
reference_answer: No, for EP1001 submissions the application-body.xml is required and must be referenced.

question: Which element in ep-request.xml groups declarations such as fee reductions or waivers?
reference_answer: Declarations are grouped inside the <ep-declarations> element.

question: Which XML element contains references to attached technical documents and their file names in ep-request.xml?
reference_answer: The <ep-electronic-files> elements contain these references.

question: Is the <abstract> section mandatory in application-body.xml for EP1001 imports?
reference_answer: No, the abstract section is optional and may be omitted if not applicable.

question: Which XML attribute specifies the receiving office in ep-request.xml and what is its fixed value for EP1001?
reference_answer: The ro attribute specifies the receiving office and must have the fixed value "EP".

question: How should file names be incremented when multiple files of the same document type are submitted?
reference_answer: When more than one file of the same document type is submitted, the character 1 in the file name must be replaced by 2, 3, etc.

question: Which EP1001 tab corresponds to filing office, language, and invention title information?
reference_answer: This information is entered in the General information tab of Form EP1001.

question: Which XML element stores the internal reference name shown in the OLF2.0 GUI?
reference_answer: The internal reference name is stored in the <file-reference-id> element.

question: What are the length and character restrictions for <file-reference-id>?
reference_answer: It may be up to 25 characters long and must not contain blank spaces.

question: How many <invention-title> elements are mandatory in an EP1001 request and which languages are required?
reference_answer: Three invention-title elements are mandatory, one each for English, French, and German.

question: Under what condition must <ep-previously-filed-application> appear in ep-request.xml?
reference_answer: It must appear only when the EP1001 is filed by reference to a previously filed application.

question: What does the lang-code attribute value "epo" signify in <ep-language-of-filing>?
reference_answer: It signifies that the filing language is an official EPO language such as English, French, or German.

question: When lang-code is set to "non-epo" or "other", what additional requirement applies?
reference_answer: A second <ep-language-of-filing> element with lang-code="translation" must be present indicating the translation language.

question: Can <ep-language-of-filing lang-code="translation"> appear on its own without a non-EPO filing language?
reference_answer: No, it must only appear when a non-EPO or other filing language is specified.

question: Which attributes of <ep-office-specific-data> define the filing office and procedural language?
reference_answer: The attributes are office, which must be "EP", and lang, which defines the procedural language.

question: Which XML element indicates a request for examination in an admissible non-EPO language?
reference_answer: The <ep-request-for-exam-art94> element indicates such a request.

question: What attribute must <ep-request-for-exam-art94> contain and what does it represent?
reference_answer: It must contain a lang attribute indicating the two-letter code of the requested language.

question: Which element must be included when filing a new EP application by the entitled person under Article 61(1)(b) EPC?
reference_answer: The <ep-art61-appl> element must be included with the earlier application number.

question: Where must the <declaration-of-entity-or-natural-person/> element be placed?
reference_answer: It must be placed inside an <ep-declarations> element under <ep-office-specific-data>.

question: What combination of conditions makes <declaration-of-entity-or-natural-person/> mandatory?
reference_answer: It is mandatory when the application is filed in an admissible non-EPO language and all applicants meet Rule 7a(2) EPC conditions.

question: Which element indicates that applicants request a fee reduction as a micro-entity under Rule 7a(3) EPC?
reference_answer: The <declaration-of-micro-entity/> element indicates this request.

question: In a divisional application, which element identifies the parent application?
reference_answer: The parent application is identified within the <parent-doc> element.

question: Which element records the generation number of a divisional application?
reference_answer: The <ep-divisional-generation> element records the generation number.

question: Which attributes describe a previously filed application referenced under <ep-previously-filed-application>?
reference_answer: Attributes include filing-date, ep-document-type, replaces-claims, number-of-claims, contains-sequence-listing, is-also-priority, and optionally certified-copy.

question: If replaces-claims is set to "no", should number-of-claims be populated?
reference_answer: No, number-of-claims must be left blank when replaces-claims is "no".

question: Is at least one applicant required in the Parties, Inventors section?
reference_answer: Yes, at least one applicant is required.

question: What must be present if no applicants are yet provided in a draft submission?
reference_answer: An empty <applicant> element with sequence="0" must still be present.

question: Which attributes are always required on an <applicant> element?
reference_answer: The required attributes are sequence, designation, and app-type.

question: Which <ep-agent> attribute is mandatory when rep-type is "common-representative"?
reference_answer: The ep-association-number attribute is mandatory.

question: Which parties may include <nationality> and <residence> elements?
reference_answer: These elements are applicable to applicants and ep-agents, but not to inventors.

question: What attribute of <addressbook> must match the procedural language?
reference_answer: The lang attribute must match the procedural language of the application.

question: What happens if the required applicant placeholder with sequence="0" is missing?
reference_answer: The submission would be invalid because the <applicants> section must always be present.

question: For representatives with rep-type="common-representative", what value must be used in the <last-name> element?
reference_answer: The <last-name> must contain the organisation name of the association acting as representative.

question: Do address detail elements that are hidden for inventors in the OLF2.0 GUI still exist in the XML?
reference_answer: Yes, those address elements still exist in the XML even if they are not shown in the GUI or PDF.

question: What is the effect of providing a <registered-number/> element for an applicant?
reference_answer: The <registered-number/> element is ignored for applicants and may be empty.

question: Which parent XML element contains <applicants>, <inventors>, <agents>, and <correspondence-address>?
reference_answer: All these elements are contained within the <parties> element.

question: Which attributes are required on an <applicant> element in the provided examples?
reference_answer: The attributes sequence, designation, and app-type are required.

question: Which element specifies the procedural language for an applicant’s address details?
reference_answer: The lang attribute on the <addressbook> element specifies the procedural language.

question: When an applicant is both a natural person and an inventor, how is this represented in XML?
reference_answer: The applicant is represented with app-type="applicant-inventor".

question: Under which conditions may an Address for correspondence be supplied?
reference_answer: Only if the Common representative checkbox is enabled and the applicant’s residence country is an EPC contracting state.

question: Where must <correspondence-address> be placed in ep-request.xml?
reference_answer: It must be a child of <parties>, in addition to <applicants>.

question: Which child elements are allowed inside the <addressbook> of a <correspondence-address>?
reference_answer: Only <last-name>, <first-name>, and <address> are allowed.

question: How many <addressbook> records may appear inside a <correspondence-address> element?
reference_answer: Exactly one <addressbook> record must be present.

question: Which attribute identifies an ep-agent as an association acting as common representative?
reference_answer: The rep-type attribute with value "common-representative" identifies it.

question: What does the <ep-association-number> attribute represent for a common representative?
reference_answer: It identifies the association acting as the common representative.

question: Can inventors include nationality and residence elements in XML even if not shown in the GUI?
reference_answer: Yes, nationality and residence elements may still exist in the XML.

question: What attribute indicates that an inventor has waived their rights under Rule 20(1) EPC?
reference_answer: The renunciation attribute set to "yes" indicates a waiver.

question: If no validation states are selected, how must <validation-states> be represented?
reference_answer: It must be present as an empty <validation-states/> element.

question: What element always represents all EPC contracting states in designation data?
reference_answer: The <region> element containing <country>EP</country> represents all EPC contracting states.

question: Where are applicant-specific designated states listed when they differ between applicants?
reference_answer: They are listed inside a <designated-states> element within the corresponding <applicant> entry.

question: When must the <priority-claims> section be present in ep-request.xml?
reference_answer: It must be present when the application declares one or more priority claims.

question: What determines the value of the search-type attribute in <earlier-search>?
reference_answer: The search-type must match the kind of the priority claim: national, international-type, or isr.
